candidate.title: Reliability of AI systems on Ghanaian languages
candidate.workingTitle: Reliability of AI systems on Ghanaian languages
candidate.summary: Can AI systems be reliably evaluated on a bounded task in a selected Ghanaian language, beyond fluent-sounding output? This remains an alternative because neither the language nor task has been selected.
candidate.shortDescription: An evaluation-centred alternative focused on reliability, meaning preservation, and speaker-validated errors in a selected Ghanaian language.
candidate.ghanaianRelevance: The subject is Ghanaian languages. The evaluation is only as good as the language choice and the speakers who check it.
candidate.technicalContribution: A controlled benchmark/evaluation set and structured error analysis for one selected language and task. No novel model or established research gap is claimed at this stage.

feasibility.rationale: This is a planning assessment. Dataset construction and native-speaker validation are heavy dependencies.

candidate.dataRequirements: A speaker-validated evaluation set for one task in one selected Ghanaian language. Twi/code-switching was discussed as a possible focus, not a final selection. Khaya AI, GhanaNLP, and Nsanku were mentioned as existing ecosystem/benchmark work to review before claiming novelty. Confirm licensing, provenance, model versions, and speaker-validation procedures.
candidate.evaluationDesign: Fix one task, language, model set, and evaluation protocol. Compare model outputs against speaker-validated references or judgements; categorise meaning-changing, factual, orthographic, code-switching, and contextual errors as appropriate to the chosen task. Report agreement and adjudication procedures. Do not rely only on automatic translation metrics.
majorRisks: A generic Ghanaian-language benchmark may overlap with existing work by Khaya AI, GhanaNLP, or Nsanku.

nodes.title: Fluent output in a Ghanaian language may still be unreliable
nodes.summary: General-purpose models can sound fluent in underrepresented Ghanaian languages while being inaccurate or contextually wrong.
nodes.detail: The discussions considered Ghanaian-language AI reliability, including the Khaya AI ecosystem. The core concern is that fluent-sounding output may still be semantically or contextually wrong. This should be treated as a bounded evaluation problem, not a broad attempt to build a general low-resource language model. No language or task has yet been selected. Twi and code-switching were discussed as possible evaluation settings, but no language has been chosen. Prior benchmark activity associated with Khaya AI, GhanaNLP, and Nsanku means a generic benchmark proposal risks duplication.

nodes.title: How reliably do selected AI models perform one bounded task in a selected Ghanaian language?
nodes.summary: How reliable are selected models on one task, in one or two Ghanaian languages, once code-switching and spelling variation are included?
nodes.detail: The research question becomes meaningful only after selecting a language, task, model set, and speaker-validation protocol. A study of “Ghanaian languages” as a whole is too broad for the stated MPhil timeframe.

nodes.title: Coverage for Ghanaian languages is not mapped here
nodes.summary: Coverage for Ghanaian languages is not mapped here
nodes.detail: Khaya AI was raised in the project discussions as a relevant Ghanaian-language AI initiative/ecosystem lead. It must be treated separately from peer-reviewed papers, model cards, datasets, and benchmark resources. The catalogue currently contains no verified publications or datasets for this candidate. GhanaNLP and Nsanku were also named in the discussions as existing Ghanaian-language resources/benchmark activity. Their exact benchmark tasks, datasets, and results must be reviewed before defining a contribution.

nodes.title: Benchmark averages may hide errors that matter to a reader
nodes.summary: Benchmark averages may hide errors that matter to a reader
nodes.detail: A possible issue is that fluent output and aggregate benchmark scores may conceal meaning-changing, culturally/contextually inappropriate, or orthographic errors. The project has not yet established this as a literature gap: a focused review of the selected language/task and speaker-validated evaluation work is required. The study must identify a narrower unresolved failure mode than “Ghanaian languages are under-resourced”; generic reliability benchmarking may overlap with existing Khaya AI/GhanaNLP/Nsanku work.
risks: Dataset construction and native-speaker validation are major dependencies.
The topic is too broad until the language and the task are named.
validationRequirements: Choose language and task before making gap claims.
Review model documentation and benchmarks separately from peer-reviewed research.

nodes.title: One task, one or two languages, a controlled error analysis
nodes.summary: One task, one or two languages, a controlled error analysis
nodes.detail: Construct or adapt a small, legally usable, speaker-validated evaluation set for one task in one selected Ghanaian language; compare a limited number of accessible models and analyse error types. Keep code-switching and orthographic variation only if they are relevant to the chosen task and can be annotated reliably.
